newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends broadly higher on spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends broadly higher on spec buying.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended broadly higher on Tuesday, boosted by speculative buying amid persistent short-term supply concerns, traders said.
"People are still inclined to buy this market because it seems there is still tightness in the nearbys," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "And it is helping the rest of the complex."

The most-active May contract rose 3.85 cents per lb on the day, to 203.15 cents, after ranging between 205.40 and 198.25. Spot March closed 3.50 cents higher, at 219.00 cents, while the rest finished up 2.20 to 3.00.

Prices bucked lower pre-opening expectations and came in higher this morning, as traders followed through on Monday's late-session rally. On Monday, May delivery shrugged off early weakness and gained a hefty 9.50 cents.
"Yesterday's activity provided a level of buying that was supportive," Platt said.

Dealers said May's inability to get through resistance at 205.50 cents sparked some local profit-taking, but steady commercial interest below 200.00 cents stemmed losses and prevented a test of support at 198.00 cents.
Although no market-moving news emerged today, analysts and traders said low inventory levels continued to underpin prices.

After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the fourth day in a row, reaching 35,083 60-kg bags as of March 10. There were an additional 18,496 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
However, with only a week left to go before the spot March contract goes off the board, its open interest was still relatively high at 1,131 lots -- or the equivalent of about 300,000 bags of coffee.
Tuesday's turnover was estimated at 9,987 lots, compared with Monday's official tally of 12,984 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640))
